main_issue: Whether and when Agent D can cook strong-smelling curry in the shared kitchen without the smell bothering the others' calls, rooms and laundry

A-B.evidence: Both opposed the smell at the start (turns 2, 5); B says timing doesn't fix it (8), and later B's door-and-window workaround (19) and A's okay to 7pm (13) both accept D's compromise. They never fully converge on one arrangement.

A-C.evidence: Both objected to the smell (turns 3, 5). A accepted the after-7pm plan (13), but C still objects over laundry (21) and only offers her laundry days (28). They never address each other directly.

A-D.evidence: A first asked for no smelly cooking (1) and D defended it (4). Then D offered to cook after 7pm with a warning (12) and A said 'that works for me' (13). A also volunteered Saturdays (26).

B-C.evidence: B and C back each other repeatedly (9, 23: 'She's right'). Both still raise laundry problems, and neither has accepted the plan.

B-D.evidence: B rejected the after-7pm plan (16). D offered once a week (17). B accepted with a shut door and a warning (19), and D said 'I can definitely do that' (20). B's laundry concern remains (27).

C-D.evidence: C objects that wet laundry will make her room damp (21). D concedes and asks for a better time (25), and C gives her laundry days (28). D proposes Saturday evenings (29), but C hasn't yet accepted.
